question: Should per-agent memory-wiki vault isolation be solved as generic agent-scoped plugin configuration, as a memory-wiki-owned per-agent vault contract, or by another maintainer-defined boundary?
rationale: The issue changes plugin config/API and sensitive memory isolation semantics, and current main has no existing contract for agent-scoped plugin config or per-agent vault routing.

options.title: Define generic agent-scoped plugin config
options.body: Add a single agents.list[].plugins-style contract coordinated with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55401, then wire memory-wiki through it as the first security-sensitive consumer.

options.title: Keep it memory-wiki-owned
options.body: Add an explicit memory-wiki per-agent vault mapping or templating contract without exposing a generic plugin override API yet.

options.title: Defer core changes to external plugins
options.body: Leave OpenClaw core/global memory-wiki unchanged and point users at plugin-side implementations until a broader plugin API plan is approved.

recommendation.title: Define generic agent-scoped plugin config
recommendation.body: Add a single agents.list[].plugins-style contract coordinated with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55401, then wire memory-wiki through it as the first security-sensitive consumer.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a plugin configuration/API and security-boundary product decision, and steipete is the strongest adjacent owner from plugin config runtime history and repository policy.
